A comparative study of the three dominant modern approaches to mathematical
foundations: **set theory** (ZFC), **category theory**, and **type theory**
(Martin-Löf dependent type theory, Homotopy Type Theory, Univalent Foundations).
The course examines each framework on its own terms and then asks what it means
to "found" mathematics at all.

## Lecture slides

- [1 · Some History and Setting the Stage](lectures/lec01.qmd) — Bolzano,
  Dedekind, Cantor, Kronecker, Frege, Russell's paradox.
- [2 · The Foundational Crisis](lectures/lec02.qmd) — paradoxes and consistency,
  predicativity, the axiom of choice, intuitionism vs. Hilbert's program.

## Notes

- [3 · ZFC as a Foundational Theory](notes/zfc-as-a-foundation.qmd) — metatheory
  vs. object theory, the finitistic standpoint, formalizing the metatheory
  inside ZFC, and the axioms of ZFC. Follows Kunen, *The Foundations of
  Mathematics*, §0.4 and §I.1–I.6.
- [4 · First Consequences of the ZFC Axioms](notes/first-consequences.qmd) —
  classes and proper classes, no universal set, the empty set, unordered and
  ordered pairs, and building the first numbers with Union. Follows Kunen §I.6.
